title: The Best Flight Tracker Apps for Stress-Free Travel in 2026
summary: Looking for the best flight tracker app in 2026? Compare five top apps for live flight alerts, delay predictions and passenger rights – including a free option.
body_text: There's a strange ritual that plays out at airport gates around the world every single day. A plane is clearly late. Passengers can see it on the tarmac, or worse, can see that the gate is still empty. Yet the departure board stubbornly reads "On Time." Airlines are often slow to announce disruptions, but the flight data that powers their own systems is available in real time to anyone with the right app . That's the promise of a good flight tracker: it closes the information gap between you and the airline, so you're never the last person at the gate to find out what's going on. But what is the best flight tracker app? That depends entirely on what you need. Some travelers want gorgeous radar maps and the ability to identify planes overhead. Others want cold, hard on-time statistics before booking a specific route. And some want an app that doesn't just tell them their flight is delayed — but tells them what to do about it, including whether they're owed money. We tested the most popular options across iOS and Android to find the best apps for tracking flights in 2026 . Here are the five worth downloading before your next trip. Stress-free flying is a download away Track flights, get alerts, know your rights, and claim compensation in minutes. Download our app Loved by 1 million travellers and counting available for: 1. AirHelp Flight Tracker: The free proactive passenger assistant Most flight tracker apps answer a single question: "Where is my plane?" AirHelp's Flight Tracker answers that too, but then goes several steps further. It's the only tracker on this list that doubles as a legal expert — monitoring your flights for disruptions and automatically checking whether you're owed up to €600 compensation under regulations like EC 261 (EU) and UK 261. But there's more. Tracking, alerts, compensation checks, claim tracking, flight insurance, lounge access, Fast Track passes, airport and destination maps and tips, baggage belt info. ALL FREE. And it clearly strikes a chord: the app passed 1 million downloads in its first year, and a lovely detail in the milestone data is the nearly half of users (46%) track someone else's journey — think of a partner landing late, a parent's connection, or a friend on a long-haul flight. It's also added a "Where is my plane?" feature that follows the specific inbound aircraft assigned to your upcoming flight, so you spot trouble before the gate screens do. Here's a list of what the app actually does day-to-day, because every feature below is free for unlimited flights, with no ads. Standout features: Email and Google Calendar sync automatically imports your bookings; boarding pass scanner adds flights instantly Live activities and destination info keeping you informed about your flight status, arrival details, and local conditions at your destination Interactive map showing your aircraft's real-time position, aircraft type, and tail number Push notifications for gate assignments and changes — often faster than airport screens Baggage belt number alert on arrival, so you know which carousel to head to before you've left the plane Disruption monitoring tuned to the 3-hour compensation threshold, with automatic eligibility check Airport maps and destination tips That last point is where AirHelp Flight Tracker separates itself from every other app on this list. When a delay crosses the three-hour mark — the threshold for compensation in most EU and UK jurisdictions — the app notifies you immediately and explains what you're entitled to . It also surfaces the reason for the delay (late incoming aircraft, technical issue, weather), which matters because airline-caused disruptions are compensable while extraordinary circumstances generally are not. The app can also scan your flight history going back three years to find claims you may have missed entirely. If you file a claim, AirHelp's legal team handles the process on a no-win, no-fee basis (free users pay a service fee of 35% only on successful claims). AirHelp+: Frequent flyers can upgrade to a membership that removes service fees, adds instant payouts (€100 sent to your account within days of a disruption), fast-tracked luggage protection, and airport lounge access when delays exceed one hour. AirHelp+ plans start from €39.99/year. Price: The app, its tracking features (including push notifications), compensation alerts, and claim tracking are all free and unlimited for all flights. The only paid elements are add-ons available with AirHelp+. Best for: Any traveler who wants one app that tracks flights, monitors passenger rights, and handles compensation claims — not just a tracker, but a full travel safety net. What's next? Every delay will count! ⏱ We're so excited about this, and think you will be too. 1 in 4 flights is delayed, which means that passengers waste around 7 million hours waiting around for flights every year. We think your time is important to you, so before too long, it's going to count towards something real — a rewards scheme. Whenever you track your flights with the AirHelp app, every single minute of delays will count for points which you can exchange as rewards. We're still shaping what those rewards will be, but expect things like free eSIMs, AirHelp+ trips, or airport passes. Stress-free flying is a download away Track flights, get alerts, know your rights, and claim compensation in minutes. Download our app Loved by 1 million travellers and counting available for: 2. Flightradar24: Visuals and data If flight tracking were a spectator sport, Flightradar24 would be the broadcast network. The app covers a wide range of transmitter-equipped aircraft and displays them on a live, zoomable map that turns raw aviation data into something fun to watch. Standout features: Tap any plane on the map to see tail number, aircraft type, altitude, speed, full route, and photos of the actual aircraft Augmented Reality mode lets you point your phone at the sky and instantly identify any plane overhead Historical flight playback (up to 365 days) and weather layers on premium tiers Near-complete global coverage , including helicopters and some private aviation Flightradar24 handles the basics too — departure and arrival times, delay info, gate data — but it's not where the app shines brightest. If you need proactive disruption alerts or compensation tracking, you'll want to pair it with something else. Where Flightradar24 is unmatched is depth of aircraft-level data: it's the app you open when you want to understand what's happening in the sky. Price: Free; the Gold plan (~$34.99/year) unlocks the full experience. Best for: Aviation enthusiasts and visually oriented travelers who want the most detailed, interactive real-time map available. 3. FlightAware: Predictive intelligence FlightAware has long been the go-to desktop tool for flight tracking, and the mobile app carries that same data-rich approach. Its key differentiator is thinking one step ahead: instead of just tracking your flight, it tracks the inbound aircraft that's supposed to become your flight. Standout features: "Where is my plane?" tracks your inbound aircraft and recalculates your estimated departure — sometimes giving you a heads-up 30 minutes or more before the airline confirms a delay The Misery Map: a color-coded overview of airports experiencing weather-related delays and cancellations across an entire region Push notifications for departures, arrivals, gate changes, and cancellations NEXRAD weather radar overlays on premium plans FlightAware's strength is predictive intelligence: tools like the Misery Map help you decide whether a connection is worth risking, and inbound-aircraft tracking can flag delays before the airline confirms them. It won't help you file a compensation claim, but it might help you avoid the disruption in the first place. The free tier is solid; premium plans add extended alert history and advanced weather data. Price: Free; premium plans available with additional data layers. Best for: Travelers who want to predict delays before the airline announces them. 4. FlightStats: The clean, professional choice FlightStats strips flight tracking down to its most functional form. The interface is deliberately minimal: a timeline view of your flight's progress, current status, gate information, and weather conditions — all displayed without clutter. Standout features: Historical on-time performance data for any flight number, so you can check a route's track record before booking Clean, functional home-screen widgets that let you glance at your flight's status without opening the app Timeline-based flight progress view with gate and weather info FlightStats isn't trying to wow you with maps or gamification. It's the app you open when you need a fast, reliable answer: is my flight on time, and what gate do I go to? The historical performance data is its secret weapon, invaluable for business travelers choosing between two connections or deciding how much buffer to leave between meetings and landing. Price : Free; premium tools available. Best for: Business travelers who need fast, no-frills logistics and want to check a flight's reliability before booking. 5. Flighty: The early warning system Flighty is an iOS only app (there is no Android version), and its main goal is to provide the most accurate flight information often faster than the airline and predict aircraft delays and schedule changes using machine learning, FAA and Eurocontrol data․ Standout features: "Where's My Plane?" shows your incoming planes for flights up to 25 hours before they're scheduled to depart, so you see if delays are building up earlier in the route ML-powered delay predictions that explain why a delay is happening: late aircraft, air traffic control, ground stops, weather Connection Assistant recommends minimum layover times and flags potentially tight connections Push notifications , including gate changes, cancellations, or baggage claim notifications Flighty Passport: a travel journal, with personal statistics, maps and annual reports The app is generally fast with delay alerts, and it also works offline and updates via basic messaging Wi-Fi while you're in the air, so you can spot connection issues before you land. The trade-off: Flighty is iOS and macOS only, with no Android version available. And unlike AirHelp, it won't tell you whether a disruption entitles you to compensation. It makes sure you know about problems early, but what you do next is up to you. Price: There is a free-tier with basic functionality, or you can subscribe to Flighty Pro, starting at roughly $59․99/year․ First flight tracked gets temporary Pro access․ Best for: iOS users who want more detailed predicted delay information and notifications than an airline app typically provides․ Best flight tracker apps at a glance: a comparison table Here's a quick-reference overview of how the five best flight tracker apps stack up across the features that matter most. Feature AirHelp FR24 FlightAware FlightStats Flighty Free version ✔️ ✔️(limited) ✔️(limited) ✔️(limited) ✔️(limited) Real-time alerts ✔️ ✔️ ✔️ ✔️ ✔️ Interactive map ✔️ ✔️ ✔️ ✔️ ✔️ Delay prediction ✔️ ❌ ✔️ ✔️ ✔️ Baggage belt tracking ✔️ ❌ ❌ ❌ ✔️ Compensation claims ✔️ ❌ ❌ ❌ ❌ Travel stats ✔️ ❌ ❌ ❌ ✔️ Android support ✔️ ✔️ ✔️ ✔️ ❌ Which flight tracker app should you download? The best airline tracker app is the one that matches your travel style. If you want to watch planes circle the globe from your couch, Flightradar24 is unmatched. If predicting delays is your priority, Flighty's ML-powered alerts and FlightAware's inbound-aircraft tracking are powerful tools. Business travelers who value clean data will appreciate FlightStats. But if you want the best free flight tracker app that does more than just show your plane's location, one that keeps an eye on your rights, alerts you when you're entitled to compensation, and takes care of the legal paperwork for you, then AirHelp Flight Tracker is the clear choice. It's the only app on this list that treats flight tracking as the beginning of its job, not the end. The feature most trackers miss: your rights Here's the gap in almost every flight-tracker list: they treat a delay as information, not an opportunity. But in Europe, a delay can be worth real money. Under EC 261, if you arrive at your destination 3 or more hours late and the airline was at fault, you could be owed up to €600 — the same goes for short-notice cancellations and denied boarding. The full picture is in our guides to flight delay compensation and flight cancellation compensation , and your rights across Europe are summarized on the EU's Your Europe air passenger rights page . A great map is satisfying. Knowing you're owed €600 — and having an app claim it for you — is the part that actually changes your day. That's why the smartest setup in 2026 is a tracker that watches the sky and your wallet at the same time. Ready to find out if your past flights are worth something? Download the AirHelp Flight Tracker app for free , and check your last three years of flights: you might be surprised by what you're owed. title: Lua Workspaces: Finally, AI your team can use together
summary: Introducing Lua Workspaces - and why we think the next era of AI at work is multiplayer. Why Every CEO I speak to is under pressure to "get AI right." Pick the model, pick the vendor, pick the flagship use case, show the board there's a strategy. The more companies
body_text: Introducing Lua Workspaces - and why we think the next era of AI at work is multiplayer. Why Every CEO I speak to is under pressure to "get AI right." Pick the model, pick the vendor, pick the flagship use case, show the board there's a strategy. The more companies we see from the inside, the more convinced I am that this is backwards. Here's what's actually happening in most companies: nearly everyone is already using AI. A salesperson has worked out a better follow-up flow - it lives in their chat history. An analyst has a research method that gets them to answers twice as fast — it lives in a Claude tab. A team asks the same question every week, and the company never learns the answer. Everyone is getting individually faster. The company learns nothing. Context does not travel. Learning does not compound. And when your best people leave, their entire AI playbook walks out the door in a browser profile. That's the problem we built Workspaces for. Not "your company needs more AI" - it already has plenty. It's that all of it is single-player. Why now Three things are converging, and they're why this couldn't have waited. The model race has made betting impossible. The best model for a given task changes quarter to quarter. Legal teams tend to prefer one vendor, engineers another, and both are right. Committing your company to a single AI vendor right now is the hardest bet in tech - and the projects we watch fail usually didn't pick the wrong model anyway. They picked the wrong use case, in a boardroom, in advance. Adoption has outrun visibility. Around 78% of people using AI at work are bringing their own tools. Whatever your official AI strategy says, your real one is scattered across personal subscriptions and private chat histories, invisible to the company paying for the productivity. The knowledge is leaking. Every prompt someone perfects, every workflow someone invents, every answer someone digs out of a model - right now it accrues to the individual and to the model vendor. Not to the company. The longer that runs, the bigger the asset you're not building. Our vision We think the next era of AI at work is multiplayer. Not a chatbot for every employee. Not an agent platform that skips the people. A workspace where your team and its AI work in the same threads, on the same memory - the way work actually happens. That memory changes what AI can be for a company. When the workspace remembers, it learns. It notices the Monday report that gets rebuilt every week, the customer follow-up that keeps slipping, the question that gets asked every Thursday. And over time, it proposes the digital employees your company should run next - grown from how your team actually works, not guessed at in a strategy offsite. And through all of it, one principle: what your team builds with AI should belong to your company. The memory, the workflows, the learning - an asset that survives every model change, every vendor shift, every departure. The companies that win this transition won't be the ones that guessed the perfect use case. They'll be the ones that turned shadow AI into company AI. What's in Workspaces today Lua Workspaces is a native app for macOS, Windows, and Linux. From day one: Every frontier model, one workspace. Claude, GPT, Gemini and more - pick the right model for the task, or let Lua route it. No vendor to marry, and you swap the moment the leaderboard changes. Work together. Shared threads and @mentions. Your teammate joins the conversation - not a screenshot of it. An assistant from day one. Every seat starts with a personal assistant that learns how you work and starts taking the tedious parts. One company memory. Conversations, decisions, and documents compound into a shared memory the whole workspace draws on - so nobody explains anything twice. Bring your history. Import your ChatGPT and Claude conversations in minutes. Nothing starts from zero. Visibility and ceilings. See what's actually being used, and cap spend per seat. The monthly number is a ceiling, not a surprise. "Auto Recruit". Automatically build new digital employees inside your business as Workspaces learns about your business. It auto-updates, and it will be updating a lot - this is the fastest-moving thing we've ever shipped, and multiplayer gets major work over the coming weeks. Early access comes with two months unmetered, and you can invite three teammates straight from the app. It's built for teams; you feel it the moment a second person joins. Welcome to the multiplayer AI era. Join the waitlist → 0:00 / 1:39

title: How to Set Up Automated Incident Triage with AI
summary: A step-by-step guide to setting up AI-powered incident triage using IncidentFox. Automate alert investigation, root cause analysis, and Slack notifications.
body_text: When an alert fires at 3 AM, the on-call engineer's first task isn't fixing the problem—it's figuring out what the problem actually is. They open dashboards, check recent deployments, scan logs, and correlate signals across services. This investigation phase often takes longer than the fix itself. AI can automate most of this work, delivering a preliminary diagnosis by the time the engineer opens their laptop. This guide walks through setting up automated incident triage using IncidentFox. What We're Building By the end of this guide, you'll have: AI-powered alert enrichment that gathers context automatically Automated root cause analysis for incoming incidents Slack notifications with investigation summaries Integration with your existing PagerDuty alerts Prerequisites Before starting, you'll need: A Kubernetes cluster (for running IncidentFox) PagerDuty account with API access Slack workspace with permission to add apps Access to your monitoring stack (Prometheus, Datadog, or similar) Basic familiarity with kubectl and Helm 1 Deploy IncidentFox First, add the IncidentFox Helm repository: helm repo add incidentfox https://charts.incidentfox.ai helm repo update Create a values file for your configuration: # values.yaml config: llm: provider: openai # or anthropic, azure, local apiKey: ${OPENAI_API_KEY} integrations: pagerduty: enabled: true apiKey: ${PAGERDUTY_API_KEY} slack: enabled: true botToken: ${SLACK_BOT_TOKEN} appToken: ${SLACK_APP_TOKEN} prometheus: enabled: true url: http://prometheus:9090 storage: type: postgresql connectionString: ${DATABASE_URL} Deploy with Helm: helm install incidentfox incidentfox/incidentfox \ --namespace incidentfox \ --create-namespace \ -f values.yaml Verify the deployment: kubectl get pods -n incidentfox 2 Configure PagerDuty Integration IncidentFox needs to receive alerts from PagerDuty. Set up a webhook: In PagerDuty, go to Services → select your service → Integrations Click Add Integration → Generic Webhook V3 Set the webhook URL to your IncidentFox endpoint: https://your-incidentfox-domain/api/webhooks/pagerduty Select which events to send (at minimum: incident.triggered ) Test the integration by triggering a test alert. You should see it appear in IncidentFox logs: kubectl logs -n incidentfox -l app=incidentfox -f 3 Connect Your Monitoring Stack IncidentFox needs access to your observability data to investigate incidents. Configure your data sources. Prometheus If you're using Prometheus, IncidentFox can query metrics directly: # In your values.yaml integrations: prometheus: enabled: true url: http://prometheus.monitoring:9090 Datadog For Datadog, provide API credentials: integrations: datadog: enabled: true apiKey: ${DATADOG_API_KEY} appKey: ${DATADOG_APP_KEY} site: datadoghq.com # or datadoghq.eu Logs Connect your log aggregator: integrations: logs: provider: loki # or elasticsearch, cloudwatch url: http://loki.monitoring:3100 After updating your values, upgrade the deployment: helm upgrade incidentfox incidentfox/incidentfox \ --namespace incidentfox \ -f values.yaml 4 Set Up Slack Notifications Configure IncidentFox to post investigation summaries to Slack. Create a Slack App Go to api.slack.com/apps → Create New App Choose From scratch , name it "IncidentFox" Under OAuth & Permissions , add these scopes: chat:write channels:read groups:read Install the app to your workspace Copy the Bot User OAuth Token Configure the Channel In your values.yaml: integrations: slack: enabled: true botToken: xoxb-your-bot-token defaultChannel: "#incidents" # Where to post summaries Test the Integration Trigger a test alert and verify IncidentFox posts to Slack. The message should include: Alert summary Affected service Probable root cause (if identified) Links to relevant dashboards 5 Add Your Team's Knowledge AI SRE becomes more useful when it understands your specific environment. Add context through runbooks and historical incidents. Import Runbooks If you have existing runbooks (Markdown, Confluence, Notion), import them: incidentfox kb import --source ./runbooks/ Or connect directly to Confluence: knowledge: confluence: enabled: true url: https://your-company.atlassian.net email: ${CONFLUENCE_EMAIL} apiToken: ${CONFLUENCE_API_TOKEN} spaces: ["SRE", "RUNBOOKS"] Import Historical Incidents Past incidents help IncidentFox recognize patterns: incidentfox incidents import --source pagerduty --since 2025-01-01 This imports incident data including: Alert details Timeline Resolution notes Post-incident reports The more history you provide, the better IncidentFox can identify similar issues and suggest proven fixes. 6 Configure Triage Rules Customize how IncidentFox handles different alert types. Create a triage configuration: # triage-rules.yaml rules: - name: high-severity-immediate match: severity: [critical, high] actions: - investigate: full - notify: channel: "#incidents-critical" mention: "@oncall" - name: database-alerts match: service: ["postgres", "redis", "mysql"] actions: - investigate: full - runbook: database-troubleshooting - notify: channel: "#dba-alerts" - name: low-severity-batch match: severity: [low, warning] actions: - investigate: basic - batch: window: 15m channel: "#alerts-digest" Apply the configuration: kubectl create configmap triage-rules \ --from-file=triage-rules.yaml \ -n incidentfox kubectl rollout restart deployment/incidentfox -n incidentfox 7 Test the Full Flow Now test the complete automated triage flow: Trigger a test alert in PagerDuty (or wait for a real one) Watch the logs to see IncidentFox receive and process it: kubectl logs -n incidentfox -l app=incidentfox -f Check Slack for the investigation summary Review the analysis in the IncidentFox UI: https://your-incidentfox-domain/incidents A successful triage should show: Automatic data collection from your monitoring tools Correlation with recent changes Similar past incidents (if any) Probable root cause with confidence score Suggested remediation steps 8 Tune and Iterate After running for a few incidents: Review Accuracy Check how accurate the AI's root cause analysis is. If it's often wrong about certain alert types, you may need: Better runbook documentation for those scenarios More historical incident data Adjusted correlation rules Reduce Noise If IncidentFox is over-alerting or creating too many low-value notifications: Adjust triage rules to batch low-severity alerts Tune the similarity threshold for "related alerts" Add suppression rules for known flaky alerts Expand Coverage Once confident in the setup: Add more services and alert sources Enable additional integrations (Grafana, Sentry, etc.) Consider enabling automated remediation for well-understood issues What Success Looks Like After implementing automated triage, you should see: Faster initial response: Engineers wake up to a summary instead of starting from scratch. Reduced investigation time: The AI has already gathered context and tested common hypotheses. More consistent triage: Every incident gets the same thorough initial analysis, regardless of which engineer is on call. Better knowledge capture: Runbooks and past incidents become actively useful rather than forgotten documentation. Troubleshooting IncidentFox isn't receiving alerts Check the PagerDuty webhook configuration Verify network connectivity from PagerDuty to your IncidentFox endpoint Check the ingress/load balancer logs Investigation quality is poor Ensure monitoring integrations are working (test Prometheus queries) Import more historical incidents Add domain-specific runbooks Slack notifications aren't appearing Verify the bot token has correct permissions Check the bot is invited to the target channel Review IncidentFox logs for Slack API errors Next Steps Once basic triage is working: Add more data sources: Connect additional monitoring tools, log systems, and deployment pipelines Build team-specific agents: Create specialized AI agents for different teams (database, payments, infrastructure) with domain-specific knowledge Enable advanced features: Dependency mapping, predictive alerting, automated remediation Measure impact: Track MTTR, investigation time, and engineer satisfaction to quantify the value Conclusion Automated incident triage reduces the cognitive load on on-call engineers by handling the initial investigation work. Instead of manually correlating signals across tools, engineers receive a preliminary diagnosis with supporting evidence. The setup requires some upfront work—integrations, knowledge import, rule configuration—but pays off in faster incident response and more consistent triage quality. Start with a subset of your alerts, validate the analysis quality, and expand from there.

title: John Mayer to Perform Exclusive SiriusXM Concert in the Hamptons
summary: Intimate performance at Stephen Talkhouse, brought to you by Uber, will celebrate Mayer’s exclusive channel, Life with John Mayer Andy Cohen to…...
body_text: John Mayer to Perform Exclusive SiriusXM Concert in the Hamptons July 23, 2026 12:00pm EDT Download as PDF Intimate performance at Stephen Talkhouse, brought to you by Uber, will celebrate Mayer’s exclusive channel, Life with John Mayer Andy Cohen to sit down with John Mayer for a special pre-show interview NEW YORK, NY – July 23, 2026 – SiriusXM today announced that seven-time GRAMMY® Award-winning singer, songwriter John Mayer will perform an exclusive SiriusXM concert, brought to you by Uber, on Wednesday, August 26 at Stephen Talkhouse in Amagansett, NY. Mayer headlines his own SiriusXM channel, Life with John Mayer (ch. 4), as the channel’s curator and an omnipresent voice on air, he has brought his listeners closer to his life and his music while sharing exclusive stories and insights into his catalog and career. August’s performance will deliver those listeners another special moment with the opportunity to hear him in his only live performance of the summer. During this can’t-miss show, Mayer, joined by his full band, will perform a career-spanning set of the beloved songs that made him a global superstar. Ahead of the performance, Andy Cohen will join John Mayer for an exclusive conversation, giving listeners a special behind-the-scenes look before he takes the stage. SiriusXM subscribers and fans can enter for a chance to win a pair of tickets to the show – click HERE for full details. If you do not live in the Amagansett, NY area, you can also enter for your chance to win a VIP trip to the concert – click HERE for full details. “SiriusXM has created a great tradition of an annual summer concert in the Hamptons, and I’m excited to be this year’s performer. I’ve had such a great time building Life with John Mayer and recording the show live for the channel is the perfect way to bring it all full circle,” said John Mayer. “John is an incredible creative partner and his dedication to music is evident as both an artist and curator of his SiriusXM channel, Life with John Mayer. Bringing him to the stage at Stephen Talkhouse, one of the most intimate music venues in the country, is exactly the kind of special experience SiriusXM loves to create for our listeners. We’re thrilled to celebrate the spirit of live music with an unforgettable show in the legacy of SiriusXM’s epic performers at this venue from an artist who continues to inspire audiences everywhere," said Scott Greenstein, SiriusXM’s President and Chief Content Officer. John Mayer live at Stephen Talkhouse will air on Saturday, August 29 at 8:00 pm ET on Life with John Mayer and will be available on the SiriusXM app. Additionally, Andy Cohen’s sit down with John Mayer will air on Radio Andy on Friday, August 28 at 10:00 am ET. John Mayer’s performance will be the latest in a series of special concerts SiriusXM has presented at Stephen Talkhouse. Artists who have previously performed for SiriusXM listeners at the famed Hamptons music venue include Brandi Carlile, Coldplay, Dave Matthews, Ed Sheeran, Jelly Roll, The Killers, Metallica and Mumford & Sons. Life with John Mayer, Mayer’s exclusive year-round channel launched in November 2023. The channel is an unparalleled musical experience curated by the guitarist and songwriter and is defined not by genre, but by the time of day as well as the day of the week. The channel features a hand-selected mix of Mayer’s favorite music, collaborations, never-before-heard material and more. SiriusXM’s Life With John Mayer is available to subscribers nationwide in their cars on channel 4 and anytime on the SiriusXM app. Eligible customers can get their first three months of SiriusXM for free. Click here to sign up and experience all that SiriusXM has to offer. See Offer Details. Sweepstakes: No Purchase Necessary. U.S. 21+ only. See Official Rules for all details. Enter by 8/18 at 11:59 pm ET. Void where prohibited. Sponsor: Sirius XM Radio LLC. ### About John Mayer There’s nobody quite like John Mayer . He has emerged as a GRAMMY® Award-winning artist, celebrated songwriter, and iconic guitar player all at once. The Bridgeport, CT native introduced himself on the quintuple-platinum Room For Squares in 2001 and has earned three #1 debuts on the Billboard Top 200 with the triple-platinum Heavier Things [2003], double-platinum Battle Studies [2009], and gold-certified Born and Raised [2012]. In addition to selling over 20 million albums worldwide and gathering billions of streams to date, he has garnered seven GRAMMY® Awards, including “Song of the Year” for “Daughters,” and has earned a record seven U.S. No. 1s on Billboard’s Top Rock Albums chart and 25 entries on the Hot Rock Songs chart, the most for any solo artist. In 2021, Sob Rock , Mayer’s eighth studio album, was released to critical acclaim, featuring the hits “Last Train Home” and “Wild Blue.” In November 2023, Life With John Mayer launched - an exclusive, 24/7, year-round SiriusXM channel curated and presented by Mayer. In addition to his highly successful solo career, Dead & Company was founded in 2015, with Mayer on lead guitar and vocals, and quickly became one of the most successful bands, playing to almost five million fans across 350 concerts, breaking stadium attendance records, and raising more than $15 million to support nonprofits and environmental and social causes. The band’s Sphere residency, Dead Forever: Live at Sphere , included 48 groundbreaking shows across two legs in 2024–2025, and in 2025, headlined three sold-out shows at Golden Gate Park in San Francisco in celebration of 60 years of Grateful Dead music. About Sirius XM Holdings Inc. SiriusXM is the leading audio entertainment company in North America with a portfolio of audio businesses including its flagship subscription entertainment service SiriusXM; the ad-supported and premium music streaming services of Pandora; an expansive podcast network; and a suite of business and advertising solutions. Together, SiriusXM reaches a combined monthly audience of approximately 255 million listeners. SiriusXM offers a broad range of content for listeners everywhere they tune in with a diverse mix of live, on-demand, and curated programming across music, talk, news, and sports. For more about SiriusXM, please go to: www.siriusxm.com . title: Treasury Prime Appoints Travis Champion as Vice President of Revenue
summary: Seasoned fintech leader joins Treasury Prime to unify commercial strategy and drive revenue growth
body_text: SAN FRANCISCO, May 6, 2026 – Treasury Prime , today announced the appointment of Travis Champion as Vice President of Revenue. In this newly unified role overseeing sales, marketing and broader commercial functions, Champion will lead the company’s go-to-market strategy as Treasury Prime continues to scale its embedded banking platform for fintechs, banks and corporate clients. Champion’s leadership will focus on aligning sales, marketing and strategic partnerships to drive more efficient conversion, accelerate customer acquisition and expand Treasury Prime’s reach across new markets. He will also build an AI-powered, scalable revenue engine to support the company’s next phase of growth. “Bringing Treasury Prime’s sales and marketing teams together under a single leader is a critical step in how we scale,” said Chris Dean, CEO of Treasury Prime. “Travis brings the rare combination of strategic vision and hands-on execution that this role demands. As we accelerate and deepen our bank and fintech partnerships, his leadership will be critical in shaping the next chapter of Treasury Prime’s story.” Champion joins Treasury Prime with over 25 years of experience leading high-performing sales and marketing organizations across the fintech and financial services landscape. Most recently, he served as Head of GTM, Partnerships & Business Development at Minna Technologies, where he led the company's North America launch and grew its cardholder reach to over 100 million US cardholders, culminating in Minna's acquisition by Mastercard in 2024. Throughout his career, he has led commercial strategy across multiple high-growth phases, contributing to successful exits and increased valuations. “Embedded banking is entering a pivotal phase, and Treasury Prime is well-positioned to help shape what comes next,” said Travis Champion, Vice President of Revenue at Treasury Prime. “The platform, the partnerships and the team here are truly best-in-class. I'm excited to help scale our go-to-market motion and bring Treasury Prime's capabilities to more banks and fintechs building the financial products of the future.” Champion’s appointment underscores Treasury Prime’s focus on scaling growth and expanding its ecosystem of banks and fintech partners as it continues to build the leading embedded banking platform. About Treasury Prime Treasury Prime is building the future of finance. Through its cutting-edge embedded banking software, Treasury Prime facilitates seamless connections between banks and enterprise partners, equipping them with everything they need to launch innovative financial products with a strong commitment to responsible practices. Beyond its core banking offerings, which encompass accounts and payment infrastructure, Treasury Prime also provides a robust partner marketplace. This marketplace offers a wide range of auxiliary services tailored to meet the diverse needs of bank-fintech partnerships. Treasury Prime was named Best Banking-as-a-Service Platform in the Tearsheet Embedded Awards 2021 and 2022, and was named to CB Insights' annual 2021 Fintech 250 list. ‍ Media Contact ‍ Taylor D’Eliseo Walker Sands, for Treasury Prime treasury-prime-pr@walkersands.com

title: Can an App's Layout Be Customized Separately for Desktop and for Mobile?
summary: Find out whether an app's layout can be customized separately for desktop and for mobile in Jestor.
body_text: Yes. In Jestor , once you enter builder mode for an app, you can switch between the desktop version and the mobile version, organizing the components independently for each one. Why splitting layout by device matters A layout designed for a large computer screen doesn't always work well on a small phone screen. Elements that make sense side by side on desktop might need to stack on mobile to stay readable. What can be adjusted separately Position and order of components in the desktop version Position and order of components in the mobile version, independently A preview of how the app will look on mobile, right from your computer The same data and features, just organized differently per screen How to customize the mobile layout in Jestor Open the app's builder mode Switch between the desktop version and the mobile version Rearrange components to fit the available space on each version Save — the app now displays the correct layout depending on the device Process automation accessible on any screen Having layouts optimized for both desktop and mobile ensures process automation keeps working well even when the team needs to handle something urgent from their phone, without needing to be at a computer. Frequently Asked Questions Do I need to build the app twice, once for each device? No, the data and features are the same; only the visual organization is adjusted per version. Can I preview what it looks like on mobile without leaving my computer? Yes, builder mode shows a preview of the mobile version right on your computer screen. Does the app work on mobile even without manually adjusting the mobile layout? Yes, but adjusting it manually improves the experience, making better use of screen space on jestor.com .
